analysis.title: US Conviction List - Directors' Cut: November 2026 Update - Mid-earnings thoughts
key_insights: GS adds Amphenol (APH) to the US Conviction List, which now holds 23 Buy-rated names. DoorDash (DASH) was removed on 10/29 after 269 days on the list, with a life-to-date return of -24.7% relative to the S&P 500.

October was bifurcated. The S&P 500 fell 0.9% and the Nasdaq Composite fell almost 7%, while the S&P 500 equal-weight index rose about 5% as investors rotated out of mega-cap tech and into 'old economy' HALO (heavy assets, low obsolescence) stocks.

The AI trade paused in October as investors questioned the durability of infrastructure spending given uncertainty in the public credit markets needed to fund projects. CRWV became a focal point of concern, and Gabriela Borges upgraded CRWV to Buy on Oct-19.

Hyperscaler investor focus is shifting from how much is spent on AI infrastructure to what it earns. GOOGL and AMZN sold off after results showed marginal misses in search and eCommerce, both seen as exposed to agentic AI disintermediation. Eric Sheridan says the agentic era is still in its infancy, and any cloud revenue shortfall is tied to supply chain bottlenecks, not weak demand.

The list's thesis for APH: data center components are about 45-50% of revenue, with industrial in the high teens, autos 10%, aerospace and defense 11% and mobile devices 5%. The CommScope acquisition in January expanded its fiber optic business, and APH raised its fiber revenue targets after both 2Q and 3Q (Oct-28).

Mark Delaney's 2027 APH EPS estimate of $3.90 is the Street high and 9% above the consensus mean. His 2027 EBITDA estimate is 10% above consensus. He expects IT Datacom to grow over 60% again in 2027, with revenue up about 30% on only a 5-10% capex increase.

APH price target is $122 (12 months, 54% upside from $79), based on 28x normalized EPS of $4.35. Risks are revenue growth, margins, US-China trade policy and M&A execution. Expected catalysts are positive Street estimate revisions and multiple expansion as the AI portfolio becomes clearer.

October's best performers on the list were HII (+18.7%, after a 25%+ EPS beat and free cash flow 3x consensus), EL (+17.7%), CSL (+16.8%, revenue growth 8.4% vs GS 4.8% forecast), CWST (+16.2%) and UPS (+15.8%, domestic margins up 60bp qoq).

The worst performers in October were CLS (-26.5%), AMAT (-23.7%), BURL (-11.3%), DAL (-3.7%) and AMZN (-3.5%). CLS fell with the AI infrastructure selloff despite a 10% adjusted operating profit beat and 2027 revenue guidance 15% above consensus. DAL faces higher fuel costs only partly offset by fare increases.

Conviction List hit rate in October was 77% against the S&P 500, 45% against the equal-weight S&P, 50% against GICS sector and 55% against GS Americas coverage. Since inception (n=135) the hit rate is 47% against the S&P 500 and 48% against the equal-weight index.

Macro: Brent is at $113/bbl because of the US/Iran and Russia/Ukraine wars, which have caused shortages of jet fuel, diesel and LNG. Jan Hatzius expects inflation to recede and sees one more Fed hike in December, with risk of another in March. He expects cuts in late 2027 or early 2028. Higher-for-longer rates could subtract a cumulative 0.6% from GDP.

GS forecasts global GDP growth of 2.7% in both 2026 and 2027, equal to potential growth, with risks to 2027 skewed to the downside. Ben Snider forecasts 2027 S&P 500 EPS growth of 18%, with tough conditions for valuation expansion.

Positioning guidance from the list: favor secular over cyclical growth (AMZN, AMAT, CLS, MSFT). Names with raised estimates after 3Q results are UNH, CLS, UPS, APH, CSL, MSFT, NXT and TPG. Midterm elections are an additional pending catalyst, tracked by Alec Phillips.

List-wide stats: median upside to price target is 32%, median upside to FY2 consensus EPS is 2%, median FY2 revenue growth is 9%, 22% of names have 50% or less Street Buy ratings, and median beta is 1.1. Top price-target upside: AMAT 72%, CLS 64%, BURL 61%, NXT 60%, AMZN 54%, with APH also at 54%.

sector_views.rationale: AMAT, AMZN, APH, CLS, MSFT and XYZ are on the list. GS favors secular growth over cyclical growth, though the AI trade paused in October on funding concerns.
CSL, CWST, DAL, HII, JCI and UPS are on the list, supported by HALO rotation and beats in 3Q results.
CFG, TPG and WFC are on the list, all with price targets above 20% upside.
UNH and VRTX are on the list. UNH is described as on the cusp of an EPS reacceleration.
BURL, EL, ORLY and VIK are on the list.
OXY is on the list as a free cash flow harvesting story, while the wars keep Brent at $113/bbl.

earnings_insights: HII 3Q26 (reported late October): EPS beat of 25%+ versus consensus, with free cash flow 3x consensus forecasts.
CSL 3Q26 (reported Oct-28): revenue growth of 8.4% versus GS's 4.8% growth forecast.
UPS 3Q26 (reported): domestic volumes grew 2% in the quarter and domestic margins rose 60bp qoq, with strong international margins.
CLS 3Q26 (reported Oct-26/27): adjusted operating profit beat of 10% versus expectations. 2027 revenue guidance sits 15% above consensus.
DAL 3Q26 (reported Oct-9): slightly below consensus, with 4Q revenue outlook ahead of consensus and a 4Q outlook otherwise essentially in line.
APH 3Q26 (reported Oct-28): record results with broad-based growth and robust AI/datacenter sales. APH raised fiber optic revenue targets again.
GOOGL and AMZN 3Q26 (reported last week): both sold off after marginal misses in their traditional businesses (search for GOOGL, eCommerce for AMZN).

Upcoming earnings with option-implied moves versus 8-quarter average actual moves: EL 2-Nov 10% vs 10%, VRTX 3-Nov 5% vs 6%, XYZ 4-Nov 10% vs 10%, CWST 10-Nov 7% vs 4%, AMAT 12-Nov 6% vs 7%, VIK 19-Nov 7% vs 4%, BURL 25-Nov 6% vs 7%.
APH 2027 estimates (GS forecasts, not printed): EPS $3.90 (Street high, 9% above consensus mean) and EBITDA 10% above consensus. The price target uses a normalized EPS estimate of $4.35.

risk_factors: AI infrastructure funding: uncertainty in the public credit markets needed to finance data center projects.
Hyperscaler returns: investor focus is moving from AI capex to the earnings it produces, and search and eCommerce may be disintermediated by agentic AI.
Persistent high oil prices and war-driven shortages of jet fuel, diesel and LNG, with upside risk to inflation.
Higher-for-longer rates could cut cumulative GDP by 0.6% through housing, consumer durables and business investment.
The HALO rotation may be the wrong way round if the AI era proves real, since it shifts away from structural growth into cyclicals.
APH-specific: revenue growth, margins, US-China trade policy and M&A execution. The copper versus fiber concern is judged to be overdone.
Downside risks to 2027 growth, and midterm election outcomes.

tension_points.bull_case: HALO companies (manufacturers, bricks and mortar) are insulated from AI disintermediation and offer a safer alternative to a crowded AI trade. The equal-weight S&P rose about 5% in October.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI era is likely to be real, so rotating from structural growth names into cyclicals 'can often feel wrong way'.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue shortfalls are tied to supply chain bottlenecks, not weak demand, and the agentic AI era is still in its infancy.
tension_points.bear_case: Public credit market uncertainty around project funding and marginal misses in search (GOOGL) and eCommerce (AMZN) made the AI trade pause in October.

theme_stances.key_argument: HALO stocks are insulated from AI disintermediation, but the AI era is likely to be real, so leaving structural growth can feel wrong.
theme_stances.evidence: the AI technology era is likely to be real

theme_stances.key_argument: Positive but decelerating growth rewards earnings growth because valuation expansion should be hard to come by.
theme_stances.evidence: a market that rewards earnings growth

theme_stances.key_argument: Copper and fiber momentum plus M&A should grow revenue faster than the Street expects.
